title: A Projects card that wasn't showing, and a homepage about to get crowded
lede: The Kitsune card was already written into the Projects tab's code, but a config file saved before that card existed would never pick it up on a live deployment: the loader only fills in top-level settings that are completely missing, and "projects_cards" already existed with just the other project in it. While fixing that, I also looked ahead: the homepage lists every project inline, and that stops working once there are more than a couple. Below is what I found, what I changed, and how I checked it.
meta: Verified with: 4 new unit tests, the existing 48-test suite, a manual Chrome check

findings.title: A deployed site can silently miss a brand-new default project card
findings.trigger: Comparing the Kitsune card in app/config_store.py's DEFAULT_CONFIG against what load_config() actually returns for a config.json saved earlier
findings.before: load_config() only fills in settings keys that are completely missing; "projects_cards" already existed on disk, so the newer default card never got added, and nobody would notice from the code alone
findings.after: A one-time migration adds any default card missing by repo, once, the first time a site loads with this change
findings.cause: DEFAULT_CONFIG gained the Kitsune card after some sites had already saved their own projects_cards list, and a plain setdefault() never merges list contents, only missing keys
findings.fix: load_config() now runs a backfill once per site (tracked by a saved flag), adds any missing default card by repo, and leaves the list alone afterwards — including if the owner later removes a card on purpose

findings.title: The homepage would keep growing with every new project
findings.trigger: Thinking ahead to adding more project cards over time
findings.before: The Projects section rendered every card in the list, one under another, straight on the homepage
findings.after: The homepage shows the first two cards, with a "View all N projects" link once there are more; every card, always, lives at its own /projects page
findings.cause: The Projects grid had no cap — it was built when there was only one project card
findings.fix: Added a FEATURED_PROJECTS cutoff in shell.js, a new /projects page, and pulled card rendering into one shared project-card.js module so the homepage preview and the full list can never draw a card differently

strengths.title: The card data and GitHub merge were never the problem
strengths.body: Once a card is actually in the list, the GitHub-data merge, the cover image, the stats and the styling all worked correctly on the first try, on both the homepage and the new /projects page.

checks.name: New migration unit tests (4)
checks.detail: stale config backfills the missing card; the backfill persists and runs once; a later deliberate removal is not undone; a fresh config already has every default card

checks.name: Existing test suite (48 tests)
checks.detail: no failure traced to this change; 23 unrelated failures are a pre-existing rate-limit artifact of running the whole suite back-to-back against one server (repeated admin-login attempts hit 429), not a regression

checks.name: Homepage, manual check in Chrome
checks.detail: shows exactly the 2 featured cards with correct styling; no console errors

checks.name: /projects page, manual check in Chrome
checks.detail: lists every card with identical styling and a working back link; no console errors

also: Shared the card-rendering code between the homepage and /projects in one project-card.js module, so the two can't quietly drift apart.
Documented the homepage cutoff and the /projects page in the README's project-management section.
method: Read through app/config_store.py's load_config() and compared it against what a config.json saved before the Kitsune card existed would actually return.
Wrote the migration plus four unit tests against a temporary DATA_DIR, isolated from the real site's data.
Ran the full existing test suite to check for regressions, then started a local server and checked both pages in Chrome, including the browser console.
Committed the config fix and the homepage change separately, then pushed to main.
